title: Microsoft Teams: latest meeting experience for anonymous join on Safari and Firefox web
summary: Pass. The roadmap supports the browser refresh and its stated scope, and Microsoft Learn supports the anonymous-join controls and licensing statements. Searches found no documentation specifying a refresh-specific switch, arrival default or separate licensing terms.

claims.claim: Anonymous participants are people whose identities Teams has not verified.

claims.claim: People not signed in to Teams with a work or school account are an example of anonymous users.

claims.claim: Teams displays Unverified next to anonymous users who join unverified.

claims.quote: When you turn on this per-organizer policy setting, meeting organizers with a Teams Premium license see the Require unverified participants to verify their info before joining setting in their Meeting options.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide anonymous-join toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Participants > Anonymous users can join a meeting.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. ... Under Participants, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -DisableAnonymousJoin $true sets the organisation-wide anonymous-join block.
claims.quote: -DisableAnonymousJoin ... Set this to TRUE to block anonymous users from joining. ... -Identity ... The only valid input is Global

claims.claim: The per-organiser toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified toggle Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false prevents anonymous join for organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: To prevent anonymous participants from joining meetings organized by users or groups with this policy, use this script: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false

claims.claim: The organisation-wide control governs unverified anonymous meeting join across the tenant.
claims.quote: To manage anonymous meeting join for your entire organization, follow these steps ... Under Participants, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: The per-organiser meeting policy controls which users or groups can host meetings allowing anonymous participants.
claims.quote: To control which users or groups can host meetings that allow anonymous participants, assign a per-organizer meeting policy to each organizer or group.

claims.claim: Learn says the organisation-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting is going away.
claims.quote: The Anonymous users can join a meeting organization-wide setting is going away.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends leaving the organisation-wide anonymous-join setting On.
claims.quote: We recommend leaving this setting On and using the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified per-organizer meeting policy to manage anonymous meeting join instead.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends using the per-organiser policy to manage anonymous meeting join.
claims.quote: We recommend leaving this setting On and using the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified per-organizer meeting policy to manage anonymous meeting join instead.

claims.claim: Meeting policy changes might take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes to meeting policies might take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: The listed controls concern unverified anonymous join; joining after email-code verification is governed separately.
claims.quote: If you turn off the organization-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting and Anonymous users can join a meeting after verifying is set to No, anonymous users can't join meetings in your organization.

claims.claim: Learn lists Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox and Safari as browsers on which Teams for Web is available.
claims.quote: Teams on the Teams for Web client is available on Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox, and Safari browsers.

claims.claim: The Teams for Web page does not identify browser-version requirements specific to this anonymous-join refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Safari Firefox anonymous join latest meeting experience supported browser versions. Read teams-client-web: it gives general Firefox latest-three and Safari latest-two desktop requirements, but no refresh-specific version requirement.
